chapter_title: Checking and Calibrating AI Agent Output
learning_objective: The learner will examine the lookup result for each of six citations and decide whether the source exists and supports the claim, exists and does not support it, or does not exist, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** citation-existence-checker
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine the lookup result for each of six citations and decide whether the source exists and supports the claim, exists and does not support it, or does not exist, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Invented Citation, Hallucination, Citation Quality (defined in Chapter 5) (all defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 5). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each citation the learner commits one of three verdicts. A verdict is correct when it matches the Correct verdict column in Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Reading the four checks is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A citation that looks complete is real. (2) A source that exists supports the claim. (3) A working link means the claim is supported. **Instructional Rationale:** Examining a lookup result against a claim is an Analyze-level action, because the learner must relate what was found to what the agent claimed. Six citations that mix real, misattributed, and invented ones teach the learner to ask two questions each time: does it exist, and does it say that. **Content:** The three verdicts: Exists and supports the claim, Exists but does not support the claim, Does not exist. The six citations (all made up), each with the claim the agent attached to it and the result of a lookup: | # | Agent's claim and citation | Lookup result shown to the learner | Correct verdict | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Claim: the deepest point of Lake Marlow is 31 meters. Citation: State Water Agency, "Lake Marlow Fact Sheet", 2025, https://example.gov/lake-marlow | The page loads and gives the lake's area and its deepest point of 31 meters. | Exists and supports the claim | The source is real and states the figure. | | 2 | Claim: rivers on plains meander more. Citation: Lopez, M. (2024), "Rivers of the Plain", Journal of Water Education, 12(3), 44 to 59. | No journal named Journal of Water Education appears in any index, and no article has this title. | Does not exist | Neither the journal nor the article can be found. | | 3 | Claim: wetlands filter pollutants. Citation: Okafor, S. (2022), "Runoff and Land Use", Earth Science Review. | The article exists and studies urban runoff, and it does not discuss wetlands. | Exists but does not support the claim | The source is real and says nothing about the claim. | | 4 | Claim: the reading is licensed CC BY 4.0. Citation: https://example.org/watershed-basics | The page loads, and its footer says CC BY 4.0. | Exists and supports the claim | The source is real and states the license. | | 5 | Claim: soil infiltration varies with grain size. Citation: Reyes, D. (2021), "Soil Infiltration Rates", Geology Quarterly, 5(2), 10 to 19. | The journal exists, and volume 5 issue 2 has no article with this title or author. | Does not exist | The journal is real and the article is not in the issue cited. | | 6 | Claim: aquifers store groundwater. Citation: National Water Atlas (2019), entry on aquifers. | The atlas exists, and its aquifer entry says aquifers store groundwater. | Exists and supports the claim | The source is real and states the claim. | **Provenance:** The claims, citations, and lookup results are made up for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The checks follow the chapter section "Invented Citation". **Rules:** Each citation has exactly one correct verdict. Three are Exists and supports the claim, one is Exists but does not support the claim, and two are Does not exist. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the claim, the citation, and the lookup result. 2. The learner chooses a verdict, and the choice is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After citation 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 citations in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [verdict]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The verdict is [verdict]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can tell a real citation from an invented one." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed citation. **Starting State:** The first citation with its claim and lookup result. The question shown is "Does this source exist, and does it support the claim?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says an invented citation is either nonexistent or misattributed, and lists four checks: search the title, check the journal and issue, resolve the identifier, and read the supporting passage.
